newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba discreet about diplomatic offensive in Latam.
newsitem.headline: Cuba discreet about diplomatic offensive in Latam.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro has dispatched senior aides on a discreet tour to alert Latin American nations against moves in the U.S. Congress to tighten sanctions against Cuba, his government said on Thursday.
The officials were sent to hand over letters from Castro to the region's leaders complaining about the latest moves.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso acknowledged this broad aim but declined to give details of the trips by Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina, Vice President Carlos Lage and Investment Minister Ibrahim Ferradaz.
Alfonso said the idea of the missions was to alert Latin Americans to the threat posed by moves in the U.S. Congress.

Robaina has travelled in the past week to Nicaragua, the Dominican Republic, Panama, El Salvador, Costa Rica and Mexico, handing over letters from Castro to leaders of those countries. Lage visited Uruguay and Argentina and was in Chile on Thursday. Ferradaz was in Peru this week.
The flurry of activity comes two weeks after Cuba angrily denounced a series of amendments headed for a vote in Congress that aim to tighten the Helms Burton law.

The law came into force in March last year, toughening an existing economic embargo and irritating U.S. allies with its provisions to punish third country investors doing business on property expropriated from U.S. citizens and firms after Castro's 1959 revolution.

Havana has described the moves in Congress as a further assault on Cuba. The U.S. State Department has said there is nothing dramatic about the amendments, which are tacked on to a far wider bill on foreign relations.

Lage met with Uruguayan President Julio Sanguinetti on Tuesday, Argentine President Carlos Menem on Wednesday and Chilean President Eduardo Frei on Thursday. Robaina met Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Friday, Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres on Monday and Dominican President Leonel Fernandez on Tuesday.

According to a copy of Castro's letter released by Costa Rica's government, he lambasted the new U.S. moves against Cuba. "These measures are aimed at reinforcing the economic, financial and commercial blockade (of Cuba) and strengthening the aggressive policies that Washington has maintained for more than 35 years against our country," the letter said.
